title: How Long After Signing Can You Register a Sale Deed?
desc: A sale deed for land in Uttarakhand must reach the Sub-Registrar within four months of signing, or it needs a fine to be accepted later.
keywords: registry kitne din me honi chahiye
why: Buyers in Haldwani and Nainital often sign a sale deed and then delay the trip to the Sub-Registrar's office, not realising the law sets a strict deadline.
keyPoints: A sale deed for land or a house must reach the Sub-Registrar within four months of signing, under section 23 of the Registration Act, 1908.
If that deadline is missed, the Registrar can still accept it up to four more months later, but only with a fine of up to ten times the normal fee.
After eight months in total, the deed usually cannot be registered at all, and the parties may need to sign a fresh one.
An unregistered sale deed for property worth more than Rs 100 generally cannot pass title or serve as proof of the sale in court.

sections.h: How long do you have to register a sale deed after signing it?
p: A sale deed for land or a house must be presented for registration within four months of the date it is signed, under section 23 of the Registration Act, 1908. In Haldwani and Nainital, this means taking the deed to the Sub-Registrar's office within that window. Missing the deadline does not cancel the sale itself, but it puts the deed's legal standing at risk.

The four-month clock runs from the date of execution, the day the seller signs, not the day money changes hands or possession is handed over. Buyers who pay in instalments or wait on a loan sometimes lose track of this date, so it helps to register the deed as soon as it is signed.

sections.h: What if you miss the four-month deadline?
p: Section 25 of the same Act lets the Registrar accept a delayed document for up to four further months, a total of eight months from execution, but only where the delay was caused by urgent necessity or an unavoidable accident, and on payment of a fine that can run up to ten times the normal registration fee.

Beyond eight months, the document generally cannot be registered at all. At that point, the safer course is usually to execute a fresh sale deed with a current date rather than try to revive the old one, since a court cannot simply extend this statutory period.

sections.h: Why does registering on time matter so much?
p: Section 49 of the Registration Act says a document that the law requires to be registered, such as the sale of property worth more than Rs 100, cannot pass title unless it is registered. An unregistered sale deed also cannot normally be used as evidence of the sale in a civil court, though it may still be used for some limited, collateral purposes.

whatToDo: Note the exact date the seller signs the sale deed, and count four months from that date.
If you cannot register in time, apply to the Sub-Registrar under section 25 before the eight-month mark, with reasons for the delay.
If more than eight months have passed, take legal advice on executing a fresh deed rather than relying on the old one.
Keep the registered deed and the registration receipt safely, since both are needed later for mutation (dakhil kharij) of the land records.

hi.title: हस्ताक्षर के बाद बैनामा कितने समय में रजिस्टर कराना ज़रूरी है?
keyPoints: ज़मीन या मकान का बैनामा हस्ताक्षर की तारीख से चार महीने के भीतर सब-रजिस्ट्रार के पास पहुँचना चाहिए, रजिस्ट्रेशन अधिनियम, 1908 की धारा 23 के तहत।
यह समय निकल जाए तो रजिस्ट्रार चार महीने और की देरी स्वीकार कर सकता है, पर सामान्य फीस से दस गुना तक जुर्माने के साथ।
कुल आठ महीने बाद आमतौर पर पुराना दस्तावेज़ रजिस्टर नहीं हो पाता, और नया बैनामा बनाना पड़ सकता है।
सौ रुपये से अधिक मूल्य की संपत्ति का बिना रजिस्टर्ड बैनामा आमतौर पर मालिकाना हक नहीं देता और अदालत में बिक्री के सबूत के रूप में भी काम नहीं आता।
